title: Raspberry Cordial
subtitle: Bright, sharp, vivid pink, the easiest summer cordial
excerpt: Raspberry cordial is made cold, no cooking. Fresh raspberry juice is mixed with sugar syrup to preserve maximum freshness and colour. Makes about 1 litre of concentrate.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Cold-process raspberry cordial preserves the fresh fruit flavour better than a cooked method. Citric acid is the preservative.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in ice cube trays for up to 12 months.

content.text: Raspberry cordial made cold,  with raw pressed raspberry juice combined with a sugar syrup,  has a brilliant, bright flavour that cooked versions can't match. The key is pressing the raspberries through a fine sieve rather than cooking them, then mixing with a warm (not boiling) sugar syrup. Makes about 1 litre of concentrate.

Put the raspberries in a large sieve set over a bowl and crush them with the back of a large spoon, pushing the juice through and leaving the seeds and pulp behind. You need about 400 to 500 ml of juice.
Dissolve the sugar in the water in a saucepan over gentle heat, stirring until clear. Remove from the heat and leave to cool until just warm, not hot.

Stir the raspberry juice, lemon juice, and citric acid into the warm (not hot) syrup. Pour into sterilised bottles and refrigerate immediately. The raw juice is preserved by the sugar concentration and acidity, not heat.

items.symptom: Cordial turns dark and loses colour
items.cause: Syrup was too hot when mixed with the raspberry juice.
items.fix: Allow the syrup to cool to below 40 °C before mixing, the vibrant pink colour is heat-sensitive.

items.symptom: Very short shelf life, ferments within a week
items.cause: No citric acid and stored at room temperature.
items.fix: Refrigerate immediately. Add citric acid next time. This cordial does not have the shelf stability of a cooked cordial.
Use a fine-mesh sieve or line with muslin. Raspberry seeds are very fine and need a proper fine mesh.

items.cause: Under-ripe or frozen raspberries with less flavour.
items.fix: Fresh, fully ripe raspberries at peak season give significantly more flavour. Defrosted frozen raspberries work but yield a slightly flatter result.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 2 to 3 weeks. Freeze for up to 12 months.
